commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36616: test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted

b469ff8fddb6594b69d564cca436b7baa8ed99bb test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  When a node restarts with extra_args it loses its original extra_args, so the `-whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` set by `noban_tx_relay` is lost and the node falls back to the normal tx relay delays.

  This changes `noban_tx_relay` to set `whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` in `extra_confs` instead, so it is kept across restarts.

  This speeds up some tests (running locally `build/test/functional/test_runner.py -j=18 --randomseed=1`):

  mempool_ephemeral_dust.py 49s -> 18s
  mempool_accept_wtxid.py 17s ->  6s
  wallet_fundrawtransaction.py 11s -> 7s

  Accumulated 1152s -> 1110s
  Wall 80s -> 75s

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36581: subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows

cf30d0a4123bb4237495f04e723ce9f706c2edf2 subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  `Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

  `CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

  This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

  _edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36465: Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests

5a4cd70547096af6247167d8dde6145a1b548642 Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests (benthecarman)

Pull request description:

  VerifyScript runs a P2SH scriptPubKey on the stack the scriptSig leaves before handling the redeemScript. The 20-byte push in HASH160 <20> EQUAL adds one item, so a scriptSig that leaves 1,000 items fails with STACK_SIZE, while 999 items is valid.

  An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.

  Add 999 and 1,000 item cases with P2SH and WITNESS, and the 1,000 item case with no flags, which fails the same way because the scriptPubKey always runs. Also add the same boundary during redeemScript evaluation, where the restored stack plus the redeemScript's pushes reach 1,000 and 1,001 items.

  The same case is added as a feature_taproot spender in #36455, so its dump can be added to the script assets (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#297).

  These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)

ACKs for top commit:
  ekzyis:
    ACK 5a4cd70547

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36465: Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests

5a4cd70547096af6247167d8dde6145a1b548642 Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests (benthecarman)

Pull request description:

  VerifyScript runs a P2SH scriptPubKey on the stack the scriptSig leaves before handling the redeemScript. The 20-byte push in HASH160 <20> EQUAL adds one item, so a scriptSig that leaves 1,000 items fails with STACK_SIZE, while 999 items is valid.

  An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.

  Add 999 and 1,000 item cases with P2SH and WITNESS, and the 1,000 item case with no flags, which fails the same way because the scriptPubKey always runs. Also add the same boundary during redeemScript evaluation, where the restored stack plus the redeemScript's pushes reach 1,000 and 1,001 items.

  The same case is added as a feature_taproot spender in #36455, so its dump can be added to the script assets (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#297).

  These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36287: build: Bump Xcode CLT minimum supported version to 26.3

fa0df9d336e80d37eab5f08b170a3255f287060c build: Bump Xcode CLT minimum supported version to 26.3 (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Now that macOS 14 is EOL (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS_Sonoma), it seems odd to still support native Xcode CLT builds on it.

  (macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 received its final security update on 06 Aug 2026: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)

  This patch will only be released in version 33.x, another 6 months out from now. Also, depends builds (and thus release builds) are unaffected. Affected devs or users are free to build via brew, nix, etc...

  This is mostly needed to get an equivalent of llvm-19-ish via CLT, see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcode#Toolchain_versions. Specifically, it will allow to use C++20 CTAD and also allow switching the project to C++23.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35919: p2p: cap maxconnections at 2,000 to reduce crash risk

b30f750de56c4e510f8af5a4dbba4e821b71a9b1 p2p: cap maxconnections at 2000 (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** The orphanage can abort when more than 3,000 peers have orphan announcements.
  The `-maxconnections` setting currently has no explicit upper bound.

  **Fix:** Cap `-maxconnections` at 2,000 with a warning before reserving file descriptors, while retaining the default of 200.
